categories.main_business_segments: Curtiss-Wright operates through three reportable segments: Aerospace & Industrial, Defense Electronics, and Naval & Power. Aerospace & Industrial focuses on engineered products for commercial aerospace, general industrial, and some defense markets. Defense Electronics provides advanced electronics and computing solutions primarily for defense applications. Naval & Power serves naval defense and commercial power & process markets, including nuclear and industrial applications.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced engineering, precision manufacturing, and proprietary technologies such as embedded computing, sensors, actuation systems, power management electronics, and surface treatment services (e.g., shot and laser peening). Production methods include material modification, machining, assembly, and rigorous testing, with processes tailored to meet stringent commercial and military specifications. The company also develops modular open systems and digital instrumentation for defense and nuclear applications.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Curtiss-Wright's key customers include defense prime contractors, U.S. and foreign government agencies (notably the U.S. Department of Defense and Navy), commercial aerospace OEMs (such as Boeing and Airbus), and operators in the nuclear power, oil & gas, chemical, and general industrial sectors. Major end markets are aerospace & defense (aerospace, ground, and naval), commercial aerospace, commercial nuclear power, and industrial process industries.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with principal manufacturing facilities in the United States (Arizona, California, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina), Canada, Mexico, and the United Kingdom. In 2024, 27% of sales were to customers outside the U.S., with significant operations and sales in the UK, Canada, Europe, and Asia. Foreign operations contributed 38% of pre-tax earnings in 2024.
categories.supply_chain_position: Curtiss-Wright primarily operates as a midstream and downstream supplier, providing highly engineered components, subsystems, and services to OEMs, prime contractors, and end users. In defense, it is often a subcontractor to primes; in commercial markets, it supplies both OEMs and aftermarket customers. The company is deeply embedded in customer workflows and supports both new production and aftermarket/maintenance needs.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company's 'Pivot to Growth' strategy emphasizes organic and inorganic growth, operational excellence, and disciplined capital allocation. Strategic priorities include expanding in core A&D and commercial markets, deepening customer relationships, and leveraging cross-market technologies. R&D investments focus on innovation in electrification, digitalization, open systems architecture, advanced nuclear technologies (including SMRs), and next-generation defense and aerospace solutions.
categories.revenue_model: Curtiss-Wright generates revenue primarily through the sale of engineered products and systems, as well as related services such as maintenance, repair, and overhaul. Revenue is recognized both at point-in-time (51% in 2024) and over-time (49% in 2024), depending on contract structure. The company also benefits from long-term government and commercial contracts, aftermarket services, and technology upgrades.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Curtiss-Wright competes with large, well-resourced companies in the aerospace, defense, and industrial sectors, many of which have greater scale and financial resources. The company holds leading or sole-source positions in many of its key markets, particularly in naval defense and specialized electronics. Competition is based on technology, quality, price, performance, and customer service, with Curtiss-Wright emphasizing its engineering expertise and mission-critical solutions.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Curtiss-Wright reported $3.1 billion in net sales (up 10% year-over-year), $405 million in net earnings (up 14%), and $529 million in operating income. The company achieved a 20% increase in backlog to $3.4 billion and a 20% increase in new orders. It maintains a strong balance sheet, with $385 million in cash and $1.05 billion in debt, and continues to invest in acquisitions and R&D for sustained growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Curtiss-Wright delivers highly engineered, mission-critical products and services that improve safety, efficiency, and reliability in demanding environments. Its differentiation lies in deep technical expertise, long-standing customer relationships, precision manufacturing, and a broad portfolio of niche, must-not-fail solutions. The company emphasizes innovation, quality, and lifecycle support, positioning itself as a trusted partner for defense, aerospace, and industrial customers.
